questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The following pedigree diagram shows the inheritance of a rare genetic disorder in a family (filled shapes depict affected individuals). Which one of the following is the most likely pattern of inheritance of the disorder?
questions.solution:
Based on the pedigree diagram, we can determine the mode of inheritance by analyzing the transmission of the trait:

1. Generation I: An affected male and an unaffected female have offspring where all daughters are affected and all sons are unaffected. This is a classic hallmark of an X-linked dominant trait. The affected father (X^D Y$) passes his affected X chromosome to all his daughters (making them $X^D X^d$, affected) and his Y chromosome to all his sons (making them $X^d Y$, unaffected).

2. Generation III: We see two more instances of an affected male mating with an unaffected female. In both families, all daughters are affected and all sons are unaffected, perfectly consistent with X-linked dominant inheritance.

3. Generation II: Affected females (who must be heterozygous, $X^D X^d$) mate with unaffected males (X^d Y$). They pass the trait to approximately half of their sons and half of their daughters, which is expected since they have a 50% chance of passing on the affected X chromosome to any child.

4. Ruling out other options:
- Y-linked: The trait appears in females, so it cannot be Y-linked.
- Mitochondrial: An affected father passes the trait to his daughters. In mitochondrial inheritance, fathers do not pass the trait to any of their children; only mothers do.
- X-linked recessive: If it were X-linked recessive, an affected father and an unaffected (non-carrier) mother would have only unaffected children (daughters would be carriers). Here, all daughters of affected fathers are affected.

Therefore, the most likely pattern of inheritance is X-linked dominant.

Answer: X-linked dominant
